chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Reading Your Tire
Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
Tire speed rating chart from L to Y, what the letter actually tests, ZR and (Y) markings, mixing ratings, and why heat and low pressure matter in Florida.
Where to find the speed rating
Look at the size on your sidewall: 225/45R17 94V. The size ends at the 17. Then comes the service description: the number 94 is the load index, and the letter V is the speed rating.
The same letter is on your door placard, next to the size the vehicle maker specifies. That placard rating is the one that matters when you buy tires. Our guide to reading tire size walks through the rest of the line.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
What a speed rating actually means
Michelin's definition: the speed rating indicates the maximum speed at which a tire can carry its maximum load under specified conditions. Continental explains how it's found: in a lab, on drum test benches, where the tire is run at progressively higher speeds under simulated loads.
Three points follow from that:
- It's a test result, not a driving recommendation. Nobody should read V as "drive at 149".
- It's really about heat. Michelin says ratings reflect the tire's overall structural integrity and heat resistance, not just its top speed capability. Pirelli describes it as the tire's ability to withstand or dissipate heat at high speeds.
- It assumes a healthy tire. Pirelli is explicit: the rating comes from a test on undamaged tires, and if a tire is old, worn down, underinflated or overloaded, the speed rating is no longer relevant.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Tire speed rating chart
These are the common passenger and light truck ratings, as published by BFGoodrich and Michelin, with Pirelli's L as the low end of the scale.
Rating
Test speed
L
75 mph
S
112 mph
T
118 mph
H
130 mph
V
149 mph
W
168 mph
Y
186 mph
(Y)
Above 186 mph (Continental)
The letters in between (M through R, and U) exist too; the load and speed rating check below covers the full scale.
Why does H sit between U and V instead of in alphabetical order? BFGoodrich's explanation: H was introduced separately, was commonly thought to stand for high performance, and kept its place when the rest of the scale was standardized.
To compare two tires' ratings, or see what a letter means in mph, use the lookup below:
It also lives on its own page, so you can bookmark it.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Z, ZR and (Y)
Older and high performance tires can show ZR inside the size, as in 245/40ZR18. According to BFGoodrich, Z was once the highest rating, at 149 mph and up, until W and Y were added above it.
Today the specific rating is in the service description. A tire marked 245/40ZR18 97Y is rated Y, 186 mph. When the rating is in parentheses, as in (Y), Continental says it means 186 mph / 300 km/h or more.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Replacing tires: meet or exceed
Michelin's rule is short: replacement tires should always meet or exceed the speed rating specified by the vehicle manufacturer. Going up is allowed. Going down is not recommended.
Michelin makes one exception: lower-rated winter-capable tires marked with the three-peak mountain snowflake symbol. In South Florida that exception rarely applies.
If someone suggests a lower rating anyway, BFGoodrich spells out what it means: the car's capability drops to that of the lower-rated tire. Its example is a T-rated tire on a car specified for V, which limits the car to 118 mph instead of 149 mph.
And remember the load index sits right beside it. Our load index guide covers that number.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Mixing speed ratings
The best answer is not to. Pirelli says it is always best to avoid mixing tires with different characteristics, including speed rating, and Continental says mixing is not recommended.
If it can't be avoided for a while, for example after replacing one damaged tire:
- Lower-rated tires go on the front axle. BFGoodrich says this applies regardless of which axle is driven, to prevent a potential oversteer condition. Pirelli puts it the other way around: higher-rated tires on the rear axle.
- The lowest rating governs. The car's capability is limited to the lowest-rated tire fitted.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Does a higher speed rating mean a better tire?
It means a different tire. BFGoodrich notes that typically the higher the speed rating, the better the grip and stopping power, but the shorter the tread life, because higher ratings tend to use softer compounds and stiffer construction. That's the same trade-off our guide to touring vs performance tires covers.
Heat, pressure and the Florida angle
Continental adds a caution that matters here: under-inflation, excessive load, and high ambient temperatures may reduce the tire's actual speed capacity. A South Florida summer, a loaded SUV and a tire a few psi low stack up against that rating.
The fix is the boring one. Check pressure monthly with a gauge, cold, and set it to the door placard, as NHTSA advises. Our guide to Florida heat and tires explains how heat affects pressure and aging.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Shopping by speed rating
- Read the size, load index and speed rating from your door placard.
- Filter tires that meet or exceed both numbers. You can shop by size and compare candidates side by side.
- Keep all four tires on the same rating where you can.
Tires ship free to the 48 contiguous states and DC. Extreme Tires installs at its Sunrise shop or by mobile van in Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach, and see installation for how that works.

chunks.text:
Quick reference
Question

What is it?
The lab test speed for carrying the tire's maximum load (Michelin)
Is it a driving speed?
No; it's a test result on an undamaged tire (Pirelli)
Higher rating than the placard?
Allowed: meet or exceed (Michelin)
Lower rating than the placard?
Not recommended, except winter-capable 3PMSF tires (Michelin)
Mixed ratings on one car?

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Key takeaways
- The speed rating is the letter after the load index, as in 225/45R17 94V. Michelin defines it as the maximum speed at which the tire can carry its maximum load under specified conditions.
- Common ratings: S 112 mph, T 118, H 130, V 149, W 168 and Y 186, per BFGoodrich and Michelin.
- It's a lab test result, not a recommended driving speed. Pirelli says an old, worn, underinflated or overloaded tire no longer has its rated capability.
- Michelin says replacement tires should always meet or exceed the speed rating the vehicle maker specifies.
- Tire makers advise against mixing speed ratings. If you must, BFGoodrich says the lower-rated tires go on the front axle.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
What does H mean on a tire?
H is a speed rating of 130 mph. It's the lab test speed at which the tire can carry its maximum load under specified conditions, not a speed to drive at. H sits out of alphabetical order for historical reasons, BFGoodrich explains, between U and V.
Can I use a V-rated tire instead of an H-rated one?
Yes, going higher is allowed. Michelin says replacement tires should meet or exceed the speed rating the vehicle maker specifies. BFGoodrich notes higher ratings typically use softer compounds and stiffer construction, which can mean more grip and shorter tread life.
Can I put a lower speed rated tire on my car?
Michelin doesn't recommend it, except for winter-capable tires marked with the three-peak mountain snowflake symbol. A lower rating also lowers the speed capability of the whole car to that of the lowest-rated tire.

chunks.title: Tire Speed Rating Chart: What H, V, W, Y and Z Mean
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
What does ZR mean in a tire size?
Z was once the top rating, covering speeds of 149 mph and up, according to BFGoodrich. Today you'll usually see ZR in the size along with a W, Y or (Y) in the service description, which gives the specific rating. Continental says (Y) in parentheses means 186 mph or more.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Reading Your Tire
UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
What a UTQG rating like 500 AA A really measures, who assigns the grades, why treadwear isn't a mileage promise and how to use the grades when you shop.
By TireDrop Team, Extreme Tires, Sunrise FL·Published Sep 30, 2026·Updated Oct 2, 2026·5 min read
Where UTQG lives, and how to read "500 AA A"
Look on the sidewall of most passenger car tires and you'll find a short line like TREADWEAR 500 TRACTION AA TEMPERATURE A. That's the Uniform Tire Quality Grading standard, UTQG for short. It's a federal consumer-information rule, 49 CFR 575.104, and it requires the grades to be molded into the sidewall.
Three grades, three different questions:
Grade
Example
The question it answers
Scale
Treadwear
500
How did it wear compared with a control tire on a government test course?
A number; the control tire is 100
Traction
AA

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Where UTQG lives, and how to read "500 AA A"
How well did it stop in a straight line on wet pavement?
AA, A, B, C (AA highest)
Temperature
A
How well did it resist heat buildup on a lab test wheel?
A, B, C (A highest)
Enter any grade string, or pick one, and the explainer breaks it down in words.
A UTQG marking such as 500 AA A gives treadwear relative to a control tire graded 100, a traction grade from wet straight-line braking (AA, A, B, C) and a temperature grade for heat resistance (A, B, C). Treadwear grades are assigned by each manufacturer and are most useful within one brand; they are not a mileage figure.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Treadwear: a comparison, not a mileage promise
The treadwear grade is the one people over-read.
The federal definition is comparative. A tire's grade reflects its wear rate on a specified government test course against a control tire graded 100. The regulation's own example: a tire graded 150 wore one and a half times as well on that course as a tire graded 100. So a 500 wore five times as well as the control, on that course.
What it isn't:
- It isn't miles. There's no conversion from 500 to any number of miles, and you shouldn't trust one if you see it.
- It isn't your commute. NHTSA's consumer guide says real-world performance "may depart significantly from the norm due to variations in driving habits, service practices and differences in road characteristics and climate."

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Treadwear: a comparison, not a mileage promise
If you want to know how long tires really last, a mileage warranty or long-term testing tells you more than a treadwear grade. Our guide on how long tires last goes there.
Who assigns the grades?
This is the detail that changes how you use UTQG. The tire manufacturer assigns the grades, based on tests it runs or hires an independent lab to run under the government's procedures. NHTSA doesn't grade tires itself. It can audit the grades manufacturers put on their tires.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Who assigns the grades?
The practical upshot: treadwear grades are most useful for comparing tires within one manufacturer's lineup. Bridgestone says the grades may be used to compare tires within one maker's product line, but because testing procedures vary, they shouldn't be used to compare one company's tires with another's. A 500 from one brand and a 500 from another don't necessarily mean the same thing.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Traction: wet, straight-line braking only
The traction grade tells you how the tire stopped on wet pavement in controlled tests on government asphalt and concrete surfaces. From highest to lowest: AA, A, B, C.
Just as important is what it leaves out. Per the federal standard, the traction grade is based on straight-ahead braking and does not include acceleration, cornering, hydroplaning or peak traction characteristics.
For South Florida, that's a real limit. An AA grade tells you something useful about wet braking. It tells you nothing about how a tire handles standing water in the outside lane of I-95 during an afternoon storm. Tread depth and tread design matter there, which is why our tread depth chart and hydroplaning guide exist.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Temperature: heat resistance at speed
The temperature grade shows how well the tire resisted generating heat when run at speed on an indoor laboratory test wheel. Grades are A (highest), B and C.
Cooper Tire gives the speed bands behind each grade:
Temperature grade
Speed band on the test wheel
A
Over 115 mph
B
100 to 115 mph
C
85 to 100 mph
Per the federal standard, grade C is the minimum level all passenger car tires must meet. So a C isn't a failing grade. It's the baseline every legal passenger tire clears.
Heat is worth caring about in Miami in August, but the temperature grade is a lab measurement under set load and pressure. Correct inflation matters just as much in real life. Keep pressure at the placard number, checked cold. Our guide to Florida heat and tires covers the rest of the heat picture.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Two made-up grade lines, read side by side
Say one manufacturer offers two models in your size, graded like this (these are examples, not real tires):
Grade
Model 1
Model 2
Treadwear
600
400
Traction
A
AA
Temperature
B
A
What you can fairly say: on the government course, Model 1 wore about one and a half times as well as Model 2 (600 against 400). Model 2 scored higher in the wet straight-line braking test, and higher in the lab heat test.
What you can't say: that Model 1 will last 60,000 miles, or that Model 2 won't hydroplane. The grades don't measure either. Still, if wet braking matters more to you than wear, and in a rainy climate it might, the grades at least show which way each model leans.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Tires with no UTQG grades
Don't panic if a tire has no grades. The regulation doesn't apply to:
- deep-tread, winter-type snow tires
- space-saver or temporary-use spare tires
- tires with nominal rim diameters of 12 inches or less
- limited-production tires, as the rule defines them
Using UTQG when you shop
A quick way to put the grades to work:
- Lock in the non-negotiables first. Size, load index and speed rating come from your vehicle placard. Our tire size guide shows where to find them.
- Compare treadwear inside a brand. Use it to rank models from the same manufacturer, not to settle a contest between two brands.
- Read traction as a wet-braking signal. Useful in a rainy climate, but it isn't a hydroplaning score.
- Treat temperature as a floor check. Every passenger tire meets C; A and B show more heat margin in the lab test.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Using UTQG when you shop
- Don't let one grade decide. UTQG is three narrow tests. Tread design, size and how you drive fill in the rest. Our post on why same-size tires cost different amounts covers the other differences.
When you're ready, browse tires, then line up two to four models on the compare page, where each tire's full spec sheet sits in the same columns. Questions about a specific tire? Call (954) 773-1896 and ask.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Key takeaways
- UTQG has three grades: treadwear (a number), traction (AA, A, B or C) and temperature (A, B or C).
- Treadwear is relative to a control tire graded 100. It's not a mileage number.
- Traction measures straight-line braking on wet pavement only. It doesn't cover cornering or hydroplaning.
- The tire manufacturer assigns the grades from its own testing, so compare treadwear within one brand.
- Winter tires, temporary spares and some others carry no UTQG grades at all.

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
What does 500 AA A mean on a tire?
500 is the treadwear grade, meaning the tire wore five times as well as the government control tire (graded 100) on the test course. The first AA is the traction grade, the highest of four for wet straight-line braking. The final A is the temperature grade, the highest of three for heat resistance.
Does a treadwear rating of 600 mean 60,000 miles?
No. The grade compares wear against a control tire on a government test course. NHTSA's consumer guide notes that real-world results can depart significantly from the norm because of driving habits, service practices, road characteristics and climate.
Is traction AA better than A in the rain?

chunks.title: UTQG Ratings Explained: Treadwear, Traction, Temperature
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
AA scored higher than A in a wet, straight-line braking test on asphalt and concrete. The grade doesn't include cornering, acceleration or hydroplaning, so it's one input, not the whole wet-weather picture.
Why don't my winter tires have a UTQG rating?
The federal rule doesn't apply to deep-tread, winter-type snow tires, temporary spares, tires for rims 12 inches or smaller, or limited-production tires.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
Tesla Tires
Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
Flat tire on a Tesla with no spare? What Tesla's repair kit can fix, when to call Roadside Assistance, and whether foam-lined tires can be repaired.
By TireDrop Team, Extreme Tires, Sunrise FL·Published Oct 1, 2026·Updated Oct 1, 2026·4 min read
First: where are you stopped?
Stuck on a highway or expressway shoulder? Call 911 or *347 (FDOT Road Rangers) first. FDOT's Road Rangers offer free help to stranded drivers on covered highways, including clearing disabled vehicles out of travel lanes. Once you're off the highway, on a side street or in a parking lot, the rest of this guide applies.
If you're somewhere off the road and out of traffic, take a breath. Then work out which kind of flat you have.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
No spare: what Tesla gives you instead
Open the trunk of most Teslas and you won't find a spare wheel. Tesla's answer is an optional tire repair kit: an air compressor that runs off the car's 12-volt outlet, plus a sealant canister. The Cybertruck's owner's manual also covers installing a spare tire if the truck carries one, but on most Teslas the kit, or a call for help, is the plan.
Tesla's owner's manual is specific about what the kit is for:
- It can temporarily repair small punctures under 6 mm (about 1/4 inch) in the tread.
- It can't repair the sidewall.
- It's meant to get you slowly to Tesla or a nearby tire repair facility, not to fix the tire for good.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
No spare: what Tesla gives you instead
And what it isn't for. For punctures larger than 1/4 inch (6 mm), severe tread damage, a damaged sidewall, a ripped tire or a tire that has come off the rim, Tesla's manual says to contact Roadside Assistance, which you can reach from the Tesla app.
Use Tesla's sealant, not any can from the store
Tesla's Model 3 manual says not to use any tire sealant other than the type in Tesla's kit, because other sealants can cause the tire pressure sensors to malfunction. If sealant has gone into the tire, tell the shop before they dismount it so they can plan for it.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
Can the tire be repaired? It depends where the damage is
A nail in the tread is a different problem from a gash in the sidewall. The industry rules are the same on a Tesla as on any car. Under USTMA guidance:
- Repairs are limited to the tread area. Punctures or cuts in the sidewall or shoulder can't be repaired.
- The puncture must be 1/4 inch (6 mm) or smaller.
- The tire has to come off the wheel so the inside can be inspected, and the repair is a plug and patch combination from the inside.
Tap a zone on the tire to see where damage may be repairable and where it means a new tire:
A bulge or bubble in the sidewall is its own case: the tire's internal cords are damaged, and it can't be repaired. Our guide to sidewall bubbles explains why.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
Foam-lined tires: repairable, with extra steps
Many Tesla tires have a layer of sound-absorbing foam glued inside the tread. Our guide to T-marked and foam-lined tires explains how to tell. People often assume foam means a tire can't be fixed. The tire makers don't say that.
Continental's bulletin on its foam-lined ContiSilent tires says:
- A trained specialist must inspect the tire and, following industry standards, decide whether a permanent repair can be made or the tire must be removed from service.
- A permanent repair needs the tire off the rim and a repair method approved for ContiSilent tires.
- That means removing a section of foam around the puncture to reach the inner liner.
Tesla's own service manual describes the same idea for its foam-lined tires: a section of foam is cut away around the puncture before the repair.
Two practical points follow:

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
Foam-lined tires: repairable, with extra steps
- Foam doesn't make a bigger hole repairable. The 1/4 inch, tread-only limits still apply.
- Tell the shop the tire has foam when you call. Not every shop is set up to repair it, and the technician needs to plan for it.
What to do, step by step
- On a highway shoulder? Call 911 or *347 (FDOT Road Rangers) first.
- Look at the damage, from a spot out of traffic. Is it in the tread, or on the sidewall? Is the tire off the rim?
- Small puncture in the tread, and you have Tesla's kit? Follow the kit's instructions and the owner's manual, then drive slowly to a tire shop or Tesla. Have the tire inspected and properly repaired or replaced.
- Anything else, or no kit? Contact Tesla Roadside Assistance from the app, or call a mobile tire service.
- Flat or losing air fast? Don't drive on it. Wait for help where you are, out of traffic.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
What to do, step by step
- When the tire is fixed, check its pressure against the door placard, and check the TPMS warning has cleared.
If the tire can't be repaired, Tesla's manual says to replace tires in pairs unless the other tire on the axle is within 2/32 inch (1.5 mm) of the new tire's tread depth. On a staggered car, the replacement has to match that axle's size.
Flat tire help in South Florida
Off the highway in Miami-Dade, Broward or Palm Beach? Call (954) 773-1896 during shop hours and the Extreme Tires van comes to the car: in a parking lot, on a side street, in your driveway or at work. The tire gets repaired if it can be, or replaced. Tell us it's a Tesla, the tire size from the placard and whether the tire has foam, so the right tire and tools are on the van. See mobile service for the area we cover.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
Flat tire help in South Florida
Not urgent? Schedule a repair or install online, or shop tires by vehicle if you'd like to order a pair in your Tesla's size.
Key takeaways
- On a highway or expressway shoulder, call 911 or *347 (FDOT Road Rangers) first.
- Teslas generally don't come with a spare. Tesla offers an optional tire repair kit.
- Tesla says the kit can temporarily fix punctures under 6 mm (1/4 inch) in the tread, enough to drive slowly to Tesla or a tire repair shop.
- For larger punctures, sidewall damage or a tire off the rim, Tesla's manual says to contact Roadside Assistance.
- Tesla's manual says not to use any sealant other than the one in Tesla's kit, because others can damage the pressure sensors.
- Foam-lined tires can be repaired in the tread area, but a technician has to dismount the tire, remove some foam and inspect the inside first.

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
Do Teslas have a spare tire?
Tesla's cars generally don't come with a spare. Tesla offers an optional tire repair kit for small tread punctures, and the Cybertruck's owner's manual covers installing a spare tire if the truck carries one. For anything the kit can't handle, Tesla's manual points you to Roadside Assistance.
What can the Tesla tire repair kit fix?
Tesla says its kit can temporarily repair small punctures, under 6 mm (about 1/4 inch), in the tread. It can't repair the sidewall. It's a temporary fix to get you slowly to Tesla or a tire repair shop, where the tire should be inspected and properly repaired or replaced.
Can a Tesla tire with foam inside be patched?

chunks.title: Flat Tire on a Tesla: No Spare, What to Do
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
Often, if the damage is in the repairable tread area. Continental says a trained specialist must inspect a ContiSilent tire and decide whether a permanent repair is possible, using an approved method with the tire off the wheel. A section of foam around the puncture is removed so the inside can be patched.
Can I drive on a flat Tesla tire to a shop?
If the tire is flat or losing air fast, don't drive on it. Tesla's manual says to use the repair kit only for small tread punctures and to contact Roadside Assistance for anything else. If you're off the highway in South Florida, our mobile van can come to the car during shop hours.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
Tesla Tires
Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
Tesla's 6,250-mile rotation interval, staggered-car limits, TPMS after a rotation, alignment warning signs, and why lifting a Tesla is a shop job.
By TireDrop Team, Extreme Tires, Sunrise FL·Published Oct 1, 2026·Updated Oct 2, 2026·5 min read
Rotation, alignment and TPMS work together
On a Tesla, three bits of routine service decide how long a set of tires lasts and whether the dash warnings mean what they should:
- Rotation moves tires between positions so they wear evenly.
- Alignment keeps the wheels pointed the way they should so no tire scrubs along one edge.
- TPMS, the tire pressure monitoring system, has to know which sensor sits on which wheel after tires move.
Tesla's owner's manuals cover all three. Here's what they say, and where a tire shop takes over.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
How often Tesla says to rotate
Tesla's owner's manuals for the Model 3, Model Y and Cybertruck give the same rule, and it's the same figure our Model Y tire buying guide quotes:
Rotate every 6,250 miles (10,000 km), or whenever the tread depth difference between tires reaches 2/32 inch (1.5 mm) or more, whichever comes first.
The Tire Industry Association recommends rotating tires at a regular interval, and for a Tesla the interval to follow is the one in Tesla's manual. Given that EVs tend to wear tires faster than comparable gas cars (see Tesla tire basics), the second half of the rule matters as much as the mileage. If you measure a 2/32 inch gap between tires before 6,250 miles, it's time.
Tesla's manual explains the reasoning: the car rides and handles best when all four tires are the same age, model and tread depth, and regular rotation keeps them wearing at the same rate.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
How often Tesla says to rotate
Use the pattern finder to see which rotation pattern fits your drivetrain and tire setup:
Staggered Teslas can't rotate front to back
Several Tesla wheel packages use wider tires on the rear than the front. Our factory tire sizes guide marks which ones. On those cars:
- Front and rear tires are different sizes, so they can't swap axles.
- Whether side-to-side moves are possible depends on the tires. A tire with a directional tread can't simply move to the other side of the car.
- Without front-to-back rotation, the two axles can wear at different rates. Check tread depth on both at every service. You may end up replacing fronts and rears at different times.
Our guide to staggered tires covers rotation, wear and buying two front and two rear on any staggered car.
Ask your installer what applies to your exact tires before the work starts.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
TPMS after a rotation or tire change
Most Teslas use sensors inside each wheel to report that tire's pressure. When tires move, the car needs to know.
After a rotation, replacement or swap. Tesla's manual says to update the car's tire configuration from the touchscreen: in the Service menu, under the wheel and tire settings. Menu names can change with software updates, so check the current manual for your car if the screen looks different.
After a wheel change. Tesla's manual says that after one or more wheels are replaced (not just the tires), the sensors relearn automatically within about 10 minutes of driving above 15 mph (25 km/h).

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
TPMS after a rotation or tire change
If a warning stays on. Tesla's manual says tires or wheels that don't match the original specification can stop the TPMS working properly, and that you should check for a TPMS malfunction warning after replacing tires or wheels. A warning that won't clear needs a technician with a TPMS tool. Our TPMS light guide explains the difference between a low-pressure warning and a system fault.
One thing TPMS doesn't do is replace a gauge. Tesla's manual says not to depend on the sensors to judge pressure, and NHTSA's guidance for every car is to check pressure monthly, with the tires cold, against the door placard.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
Signs your Tesla needs an alignment
Tesla's manual says to have the wheel alignment checked if you notice:
- Uneven wear on one side of a tire, the inner or outer edge wearing faster than the rest, or wear that's abnormally fast.
- The car pulling left or right while you hold the steering wheel straight.
Other moments worth an alignment check: after a hard pothole or curb hit, after suspension work, and when you fit a new set of tires so they start out even. An off-center steering wheel when driving straight is also a reason to have it looked at.
Alignment needs a proper alignment rack. At Extreme Tires it's done at the Sunrise shop, not from the mobile van.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
Lifting a Tesla: leave it to a shop
A tire rotation means lifting the car, and a Tesla is not a car to put on a scissor jack in the driveway. Tesla's owner's manuals carry specific warnings:
- Only Tesla's approved lift points. The manual says never to put lift pads under the battery or the side rails. The battery pack sits under the floor, and lifting in the wrong place can damage it.
- Jack Mode on air-suspension cars. On cars with air suspension, the manual says Jack Mode has to be turned on before lifting. Otherwise the car may try to level itself, which Tesla warns can cause serious damage, injury or death.
- Never lift while the charge cable is connected, even if the car isn't charging.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
Lifting a Tesla: leave it to a shop
We're not going to give step-by-step lifting instructions here. The right lift points and pad type vary by model, and the consequences of getting it wrong are serious. Have a tire shop or Tesla service lift the car, and if you're curious how it's done, read the lifting section of your own owner's manual.

Key takeaways
- Tesla's owner's manuals say to rotate every 6,250 miles (10,000 km), or sooner if tread depths differ by 2/32 inch or more.
- On a staggered Tesla, front and rear sizes differ, so tires can't move between axles.
- After a rotation or tire change, Tesla's manual says to update the tire configuration on the touchscreen.
- Per Tesla, TPMS sensors relearn on their own after a wheel change once the car has been driven for a short time.
- Tesla's manual lists uneven wear on one side of a tire and a car that pulls as signs to have the alignment checked.
- Tesla warns against lifting on the battery or side rails and requires Jack Mode on air-suspension cars. Leave lifting to a shop.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Rotation, Alignment and TPMS
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
How often should I rotate my Tesla's tires?
Tesla's owner's manuals say every 6,250 miles (10,000 km), or whenever the tread depth difference between tires reaches 2/32 inch (1.5 mm) or more, whichever comes first.
Can you rotate staggered Tesla tires?
Not front to back. On a staggered car the rear tires are a different size from the fronts, so they can't swap axles. Ask your installer what applies to your exact setup, and check tread depth on both axles at each service.
How do I reset TPMS after rotating Tesla tires?
Tesla's manual says to update the tire configuration from the touchscreen after tires are rotated, replaced or swapped, from the Service menu's wheel and tire settings. Menu names change with software updates, so follow the current manual for your car. After a wheel change, the sensors relearn automatically after a short drive.

Where are the jack points on a Tesla?

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
Tesla Tires
Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
What the T0, T1 and T2 marks on Tesla tires mean, how sound-absorbing foam works, and what changes when you choose a tire without the Tesla mark.
By TireDrop Team, Extreme Tires, Sunrise FL·Published Oct 1, 2026·Updated Oct 1, 2026·5 min read
Two things on a Tesla tire that other cars rarely have
Look closely at the sidewall of a factory tire on a Tesla and you'll often find a small code next to the size: T0, T1 or T2. Look inside it, if you ever see one off the wheel, and you may find a band of foam glued around the inner liner.
Neither one changes the size you need. But both change what you're buying, and the foam changes how a tire gets repaired. Here's what each one is, in Tesla's and the tire makers' own words.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
What the T mark means
Tesla's owner's manuals say you can identify a Tesla-approved tire by a T mark on the sidewall, for example T0, T1 or T2. Tesla describes these tires as designed to work with the vehicle, optimizing performance, reliability and durability.
Tesla's tires page explains the numbering:
- T0 marks the first version of a Tesla-designed tire.
- T1, T2 and so on mark later updates that add new tuning or technology.
Tesla also says these tires are engineered with tire manufacturers to deliver its targets for range efficiency, ride comfort, handling and noise.
So a T mark tells you two things: the tire maker built that version to Tesla's targets for your type of car, and the number tells you which version it is. It doesn't make a tire a different size or load rating from a tire without it.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
The mark isn't a size
A Michelin, Pirelli, Continental or other tire can exist in your size with and without a T mark. They're different versions of the tire, and they're tuned differently. When you shop, check that the T-marked version is actually available in your size before assuming it is.
What acoustic foam does
A tire is a hollow ring of air, and that air resonates as the tire rolls over the road. Goodyear calls this tire air cavity resonance and names it one of the key contributors to cabin noise. In an EV, with no engine to cover it, you hear it more.
The fix most tire makers use is a layer of open-cell polyurethane foam bonded to the inside of the tread. It absorbs that resonance before it reaches the cabin. Tesla says it uses acoustic foam and optimized tread patterns in Tesla-designed tires to dampen road noise, and its tires page puts the effect at 6 decibels at 200 Hz.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
What acoustic foam does
Tire makers sell their own versions, under their own names:
Tire maker
What they call it
What the maker says it does
Continental
ContiSilent
A polyurethane foam layer inside the tread absorbs vibrations so less noise reaches the cabin
Pirelli
Pirelli Noise Cancelling System (PNCS)
A sound-absorbing foam insert fixed to the inner wall reduces cavity noise
Michelin
Michelin Acoustic
A custom polyurethane foam reduces perceptible road noise
Goodyear
SoundComfort Technology
An acoustic barrier inside the tire reduces air cavity resonance
Each maker's noise figures come from its own testing, in its own conditions, so they aren't directly comparable with each other.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
How to tell if a tire has foam
Foam is offered on some sizes of a tire line and not others. To check:
- Look on the sidewall for the maker's foam name or symbol.
- Look up the exact size on the tire maker's product page.
- Ask the seller to confirm it for your exact size before you order.
What changes with a tire that isn't T-marked
This is the question most Tesla owners ask when they price replacements. Tesla's recommendation is a Tesla-approved tire. Here's what changes when you pick something else, so you can decide what matters to you.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
What changes with a tire that isn't T-marked
What stays the same. The rules for size, load and speed don't change. Tesla's manual says to use tires and wheels that match the original specification. That means the same size (front and rear on a staggered car), a load index at or above the original, including any XL or HL marking, and a speed rating at or above the original. Tesla's manual also notes that tires that don't match the original specification can affect the tire pressure monitoring system.
What can change:
- Noise. A tire without foam, or with a different tread pattern, can be louder in the cabin. Whether you notice depends on the tire, the road and your ears.
- Range. The T-marked version was tuned to Tesla's range targets. Another tire may have more or less rolling resistance. The tire maker's product page usually says whether a tire is designed for low rolling resistance.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
What changes with a tire that isn't T-marked
- Ride and handling. Tesla tunes its tires for ride comfort and handling on its cars. A different tire can feel different, firmer or softer, sharper or more relaxed.
- Wet grip and tread life. These can go either way. Some replacement tires put more weight on wet grip or tread life than on range.
Many tire makers now sell EV-specific lines that aim at the same targets: weight, torque, noise and rolling resistance. Our guide to Tesla tire types for South Florida names examples from the makers' own pages.
One more practical point: replace in pairs. Two different tires on the same axle can grip, wear and sound differently. Tesla's manual says to replace all four tires when a set is worn, and to replace in pairs when a tire has to be replaced early, unless the other tires are within 2/32 inch (1.5 mm) of the new tire's tread depth.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
Foam changes how a repair is done
Foam doesn't stop a nail, and it isn't a sealant. Continental's ContiSilent bulletin says so directly: the foam is for noise, not puncture repair.
What it changes is the repair itself. Continental says a trained specialist must inspect the tire carefully and, under industry standards, decide whether a permanent repair can be made or the tire must be removed from service. A permanent repair means taking the tire off the wheel and using a method approved for ContiSilent tires, which involves removing a section of foam around the puncture so the inside can be patched.
The usual industry limits still apply on top of that. Under USTMA repair guidance, repairs are limited to the tread area, for punctures no larger than 1/4 inch (6 mm), with the tire dismounted and inspected from the inside. Our guide to plug vs patch explains why.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
Foam changes how a repair is done
The practical takeaway: tell the shop your tire has foam before they start. Not every shop is set up for it.
Shop for your Tesla's tires
Ready to compare tires? Shop tires by vehicle, choose your Tesla, and check the product details for a T mark or foam. Tires ship free to the 48 contiguous states and DC, or free to our Sunrise shop, where installation is charged per tire. In South Florida, mobile installation covers Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach, and you can schedule service online. Have a foam-lined tire with a nail in it? Call (954) 773-1896 and tell us the tire before you book.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
Key takeaways
- A T mark (T0, T1, T2 and so on) on the sidewall identifies a Tesla-approved tire, per Tesla's owner's manuals.
- Tesla says T0 is the first version of a Tesla-designed tire, and later updates are marked T1, T2 and so on.
- Tesla uses acoustic foam and tuned tread patterns in Tesla-designed tires to dampen road noise.
- Several tire makers sell their own foam-lined tires under names like ContiSilent, Pirelli Noise Cancelling System and Michelin Acoustic.
- Choosing a tire without the T mark changes how the tire was tuned for the car, not the size, load and speed rating you have to match.
- Foam-lined tires can need a different repair procedure, so tell the shop before a repair.

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
What does T0 or T1 mean on a Tesla tire?
It's Tesla's approval mark. Tesla's owner's manuals say a Tesla-approved tire can be identified by a T mark on the sidewall, such as T0, T1 or T2. Tesla's tires page says T0 marks the first version of a Tesla-designed tire, and later versions with new tuning or technology are marked T1, T2 and so on.
Do I have to buy T-marked tires for my Tesla?
Tesla recommends Tesla-approved tires. What changes with a tire that lacks the mark is that it wasn't tuned with Tesla for your car, so noise, ride, handling and range can differ. Whatever you choose, Tesla's manual says to match the original size, load index and speed rating.
How do I know if my tires have foam inside?

chunks.title: Tesla-Marked Tires: T0, T1 and Acoustic Foam Explained
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
Look on the sidewall for the tire maker's foam name or symbol, such as ContiSilent, PNCS or Acoustic, and check the tire maker's product page for your exact size. A T marking alone doesn't tell you, because foam is offered on some sizes and not others.
Can foam-lined tires be repaired?
Continental says a trained specialist must inspect a ContiSilent tire and decide whether a permanent repair can be made, using a method approved for ContiSilent tires with the tire off the wheel. Part of the foam has to be removed around the puncture first. The usual industry limits on where and how big a repair can be still apply.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Tesla Tires
Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
Why tires work harder on a Tesla: battery weight, instant torque, the low rolling resistance trade-off, cabin noise, and why EV tires tend to wear faster.
By TireDrop Team, Extreme Tires, Sunrise FL·Published Oct 1, 2026·Updated Oct 2, 2026·5 min read
Why a Tesla is hard on tires
A tire on a Tesla does the same basic job as a tire on any car: it carries the weight, grips the road and soaks up bumps. What changes is how much of each it has to do.
Michelin sums up the difference in a few points. EVs are heavier than comparable gas vehicles, they deliver instant torque, they use regenerative braking to recharge on deceleration, and they're quiet, so tire noise is easier to hear. On top of that, carmakers want tires with low rolling resistance to stretch range.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Why a Tesla is hard on tires
Each of those pulls a tire in a slightly different direction. Here's what each one means for you.
Weight: the load rating matters more
Battery packs are heavy. Hankook says battery weight can make an EV up to 30% heavier than a comparable gas vehicle. Michelin puts it simply: vehicle weight is a critical factor in how fast a tire wears, and more weight means faster wear.
Weight also decides which tires can go on the car at all. Every tire has a load index, the number after the size, that says how much weight it's built to carry at its maximum pressure. Some EV tires also carry an XL (extra load) or HL (high load) marking. Michelin explains that an HL tire carries more load than an XL tire of the same size at the same inflation pressure. Our XL vs SL guide explains how load markings and pressure work together.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Weight: the load rating matters more
The rule for replacements is the same on every car: match or exceed the load index your vehicle was specified with. Tesla's manual says to use tires that match the original specification. You'll find yours on the Tire and Loading Information placard on the door pillar and in the owner's manual.
Check a replacement tire's load index and speed rating against your current one here:

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Instant torque and regenerative braking
An electric motor delivers its torque the moment you press the pedal. Michelin points out that this is what gives EVs their quick acceleration, and that EVs combine it with regenerative braking, which slows the car by turning the motor into a generator.
For the tread, that means force going through the contact patch both when you speed up and when you lift off. Continental describes the result plainly: tires on EVs carry a heavier load and have to withstand high instant torque, which leads to higher wear, so they need stronger construction and tougher compounds.
How you drive changes how much of that force the tread sees. Frequent hard launches put more of it through the tires than smooth starts do. Uneven wear between positions is one reason Tesla publishes a specific rotation interval (more on that below).

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Low rolling resistance: range has a price
Rolling resistance is the energy a tire uses up as it flexes and rolls. Lower rolling resistance means more of the battery goes to moving the car, which is why EV makers ask for it. Continental says the right tire can help battery range, and Hankook says EV-specific tires are designed to minimize rolling resistance.
The catch is that rolling resistance, wet grip and tread life pull against each other. Michelin is direct about it: carmakers often prioritize range when optimizing original-equipment tires for an EV, and that comes with trade-offs such as less grip or greater tire wear.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Low rolling resistance: range has a price
That doesn't make a low rolling resistance tire a bad choice. It means you should know what a tire was optimized for before you buy it. If most of your driving is wet South Florida highway, wet grip may matter more to you than the last few miles of range. Our guide to Tesla tire types for South Florida walks through that trade-off.
Noise: why you hear your tires more
A gas engine hides a lot of road noise. Take it away and the tires become one of the loudest things you hear. Michelin notes that because EVs make less noise, the sound of the tire meeting the road is more intrusive.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Noise: why you hear your tires more
Tire makers tackle this two ways: tread patterns tuned to be quieter, and sound-absorbing foam bonded inside the tire. Tesla says it uses acoustic foam and optimized tread patterns in Tesla-designed tires to dampen road noise. Michelin, Continental, Pirelli and Goodyear all make their own versions.
Foam changes a few things when a tire needs a repair, so it's worth knowing whether yours has it. Our guide to Tesla-marked and foam-lined tires covers what to look for.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Why EV tires wear faster, and what helps
Put the pieces together and you get the headline number. Michelin says that, on average, EVs wear out a tire about 20% faster than a comparable gas vehicle. Hankook gives the same figure and adds that the wear is often uneven on tires that weren't designed for EVs.
Tire makers are responding. Michelin says its newer tire lines are engineered with more wear potential to offset that 20%, and Hankook describes EV tires built to spread contact pressure more evenly.
Whatever tire you run, the habits that stretch tread life are the same ones USTMA recommends for every car:
- Pressure. Check it monthly with a gauge, with the tires cold, against the door placard. Tesla's manual says not to depend on the tire pressure monitoring system to judge pressures: keeping them correct is the driver's job.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Why EV tires wear faster, and what helps
- Rotation. Tesla's manual gives a specific interval for its cars. See Tesla tire rotation, alignment and TPMS.
- Alignment. Uneven wear on one edge, or a car that pulls, are signs to have it checked.
- Tread depth. Measure several grooves on every tire. Our tread depth chart explains the 2/32 and 4/32 lines.

Get the right tires on your Tesla
When you know what you need, shop tires by vehicle and pick your Tesla. Tires ship free to the 48 contiguous states and DC, or free to our Sunrise shop, where installation is charged per tire. In South Florida, mobile installation covers Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach, and you can schedule service online for an install, rotation or TPMS check. Questions about a specific tire? chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Key takeaways
- Michelin says EVs are heavier than comparable gas cars, and more weight means faster tire wear.
- Michelin and Hankook both put the average at about 20% faster wear on an EV than on a comparable gas vehicle.
- Instant torque and regenerative braking load the tread on every launch and every slowdown, per Michelin.
- Low rolling resistance helps range, but Michelin notes it can come with less grip or more wear.
- With no engine sound to cover it, tire noise is easier to hear, which is why Tesla uses acoustic foam in Tesla-designed tires.
- On any replacement, match the load index, including an XL or HL marking, from your door placard or owner's manual.

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
Do Teslas need special tires?
Tesla's manual says to use tires that match the original specification for your car: size, load index and speed rating. Tesla recommends Tesla-approved tires, which carry a T marking. Tire makers also sell EV-specific lines built around weight, torque, noise and rolling resistance. Start from the specification, then weigh those features.
Why do Tesla tires wear out so fast?
Michelin and Hankook both say tires on EVs wear about 20% faster on average than on comparable gas vehicles. Michelin points to extra weight, instant torque and regenerative braking. Pressure, rotation and alignment also play a part, as they do on any car.
What does HL mean on a tire?

chunks.title: Tesla Tire Basics: What's Different About EV Tires
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
HL stands for High Load. Michelin explains that an HL tire carries more load than an XL (extra load) tire of the same size at the same inflation pressure. Some heavier EVs are specified with HL tires, so check what your car calls for.
Do low rolling resistance tires really help range?
Lower rolling resistance means less energy is spent turning the tires, which is why carmakers often specify it for EVs. Michelin notes the trade-offs: a tire tuned mainly for range can give up some grip or tread life.

chunks.title: Tesla Factory Tire Sizes by Model and Wheel
chunks.text:
Tesla Tires
Tesla Factory Tire Sizes by Model and Wheel
Tesla factory tire sizes for Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X and Cybertruck by wheel option, which setups are staggered, and where to confirm yours.
By TireDrop Team, Extreme Tires, Sunrise FL·Published Oct 1, 2026·Updated Oct 1, 2026·5 min read
Start at the door pillar, not this page
There's no single "Tesla tire size," and there isn't even one size per model. Tesla fits different sizes to different wheel packages, has changed them across model years, and on several cars uses wider tires on the rear than the front.
So before you trust any table, including ours, check your car:
- Door-jamb placard. The Tire and Loading Information label on the door pillar lists the original tire size, load and cold pressure for your car.

chunks.title: Tesla Factory Tire Sizes by Model and Wheel
chunks.text:
Start at the door pillar, not this page
- Owner's manual. The Wheel and Tire Specifications section lists every factory size, with the load index and speed rating for each.
- The tires on the car. Good for confirming, but if a previous owner changed wheels, they may not match the placard.
Type the size from your placard into the decoder to see what every part of it means:
Reading the placard on a Tesla
The placard lists the original tire size, the cold inflation pressure, and the maximum combined weight of occupants and cargo. On a staggered car it shows two sizes: one for the front axle and one for the rear. Read both, and note which is which before you shop.
Two things can trip you up:

chunks.title: Tesla Factory Tire Sizes by Model and Wheel
chunks.text:
Reading the placard on a Tesla
- The placard reflects how the car left the factory. If the car has had a wheel upgrade, a winter set or a previous owner's choice of wheels, what's on the car now may differ. In that case, the placard and manual still tell you what Tesla specified.
- Pressures are tied to the original tires. Tesla's manual says tire pressures vary with the type of tire fitted. Use the figure on the placard for the factory size, and ask your installer if you've changed sizes.

chunks.title: Tesla Factory Tire Sizes by Model and Wheel
chunks.text:
How to read the tables below
The sizes below come from the Wheel and Tire Specifications pages in Tesla's owner's manuals, as published on the date of this guide. Tesla updates these pages, so:
- "Square" means the same size on all four wheels.
- "Staggered" means the rear tires are a different (wider) size from the fronts.
- Where a year, trim or wheel isn't listed, we couldn't confirm it from a Tesla page. Check your door-jamb placard.
We've left out load indexes and speed ratings on purpose. They vary by the exact tire Tesla specified for your car, and the manual lists the minimum for each. Match or exceed what yours shows.

chunks.text:
What staggered means for you
If your Tesla is staggered, three things change:
- Rotation is limited. Front and rear tires are different sizes, so they can't swap axles. Our rotation, alignment and TPMS guide covers what that means for Tesla's rotation interval.
- You buy in pairs of two sizes. A full set is two fronts and two rears, so search for both placard sizes.
- Axles can wear at different rates. Without rotation to even things out, check tread depth on the front and rear tires separately rather than assuming they wear together.

chunks.title: Tesla Factory Tire Sizes by Model and Wheel
chunks.text:
Size is only half the match
Tesla's manual is direct: use tires and wheels that match the original specification. It also warns that tires that don't match can affect how the tire pressure monitoring system works. USTMA gives the same advice for every vehicle: match the placard's size, load-carrying capacity and speed rating.
In practice, that means checking three things on any replacement:
- Size, front and rear, exactly as on the placard.
- Load index, including any XL or HL marking, at or above the original.
- Speed rating, at or above the original.
Our guide to reading a tire size explains each part, and Tesla tire basics explains why load ratings matter more on a heavy EV.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
Tesla Tires
Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
EV-specific touring, all-season and summer performance tires for a Tesla in South Florida, and how to weigh wet grip, tread life, noise and range.
By TireDrop Team, Extreme Tires, Sunrise FL·Published Oct 1, 2026·Updated Oct 1, 2026·5 min read
No top-five list here
Search for the best tires for a Tesla and you'll find ranked lists. This isn't one. We don't rank brands or products, and a list that ignores your size, your driving and what you care about most isn't much use anyway.
What this guide does is explain the categories of tire that make sense on a Tesla in South Florida, name EV-specific lines as examples from the tire makers' own pages, and show you how to weigh the four things that matter most here: wet grip, tread life, noise and range.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
No top-five list here
One rule comes before all of it: the tire has to match your Tesla's size, load index and speed rating, front and rear. Our Tesla factory tire sizes guide shows where to find them.
What South Florida asks of a tire
Snow isn't part of the picture. What South Florida driving actually throws at a tire is:
- Rain. Heavy afternoon storms put standing water on I-95, the Turnpike and the Sawgrass. Wet braking and water clearance matter more here than winter grip.
- Heat. Hot pavement and summer sun raise tire temperature and pressure. Our guide to Florida heat and tires covers what NHTSA says about heat and aging.
- Long, flat highway miles, where noise and range are noticeable every day.
On a Tesla, add the EV demands from our Tesla tire basics guide: extra weight, instant torque and a quiet cabin.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
EV-specific touring and all-season tires
These are built around what EVs ask of a tire. Examples from the makers' own pages:
- Hankook iON evo AS. Hankook describes it as a grand touring all-season tire for EV drivers, designed for EV weight and lower rolling resistance.
- Bridgestone Turanza EV. Bridgestone describes it as a grand touring tire for premium EVs, using its ENLITEN technology to reduce rolling resistance, with a tread designed to reduce road noise.
- Goodyear ElectricDrive 2. Goodyear describes it as an all-season EV tire with improved rolling resistance and SoundComfort foam to reduce cabin noise, offered in sizes for Tesla models among others.
- Pirelli Elect. Rather than one tire, Pirelli uses an Elect marking on versions of its P Zero, Scorpion and Cinturato lines developed for electric vehicles, focused on rolling resistance, noise and grip.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
EV-specific touring and all-season tires
- Continental. Continental marks tire models designed for EVs with an EV-Compatible logo on the sidewall.
These names are examples, not recommendations. Availability depends on your exact size.
Regular all-season tires
A standard all-season tire can fit a Tesla as long as it matches the size, load index (including any XL or HL marking) and speed rating. It may not have foam or EV-specific tuning, so it can be louder or use a little more range. Check the tire maker's page for those details.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
Summer performance tires
Michelin says summer tires are designed for warm conditions, above 45°F, and deliver their best grip and handling on dry and wet roads in that range. Below 45°F, Michelin says the compound hardens and grip drops on every surface. In South Florida, most driving is well above that. If you take the car north in winter, factor it in.
The EV example here is the Michelin Pilot Sport EV, which Michelin describes as engineered for electric sports cars, with low rolling resistance and Michelin Acoustic foam. Some factory Tesla packages also come on summer tires.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
How to weigh wet grip, tread life, noise and range
You can't max out all four. Michelin is direct about it: carmakers often prioritize range when optimizing original-equipment EV tires, and that comes with trade-offs such as less grip or greater tire wear. So decide what matters most to you, then read each tire's specs with that in mind.
What you care about
What to look at
Where to find it
Wet grip
UTQG traction grade (AA, A, B, C) and the tire's category
Sidewall; tire maker's page
Tread life
UTQG treadwear grade, compared within one brand; mileage warranty terms

A few notes on reading those numbers, per NHTSA's UTQG guide:

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
How to weigh wet grip, tread life, noise and range
- The traction grade comes from a straight-line braking test on wet pavement. It doesn't measure cornering grip or hydroplaning.
- The treadwear grade is assigned by the manufacturer and is most useful for comparing tires from the same brand.
- The temperature grade (A, B, C) reflects a tire's resistance to heat.
Our UTQG guide explains all three in detail.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
Tread depth matters more than the label in the rain
Whatever you buy, wet grip fades as tread wears. Our tread depth chart explains the 2/32 inch replacement line and why Consumer Reports' testing supports considering replacement at 4/32 inch for wet roads. On a Tesla, which tends to wear tires faster, measure every tire at each rotation.
Keep pressure right in the heat
The best tire for the job still needs the right pressure. Tire pressure rises with temperature and falls when it cools, so a reading in a hot driveway at 3 p.m. isn't the same as one at 7 a.m. Set pressure cold, to the figure on your Tesla's door placard, and check it monthly. Under-inflated tires also roll with more resistance, which costs range.
See how much the pressure in your tires moves between a cool morning and a hot afternoon:

chunks.text:
Shop and install tires for your Tesla
When you've decided what matters most, shop tires by vehicle and choose your Tesla to see the sizes it takes. Tires ship free to the 48 contiguous states and DC, or free to our Sunrise shop, where installation is charged per tire. In South Florida, our mobile installation vans cover Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach, and you can schedule an install online. Want to talk through the trade-offs for your driving? Call (954) 773-1896.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
Key takeaways
- Start from your Tesla's placard size, load index and speed rating. The category comes second.
- Tire categories that suit a Tesla in South Florida: EV-specific touring or all-season, regular all-season, and summer performance.
- Michelin says summer tires are designed for temperatures above 45°F, which covers most South Florida driving.
- Wet grip, tread life, noise and range pull against each other. Decide which matters most to you before you compare tires.
- The UTQG traction grade reflects straight-line wet braking, and the treadwear grade is best compared within one brand.
- Heat moves tire pressure. Set pressure cold, to the door placard, and check it monthly.

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
What type of tire is best for a Tesla in Florida?
There's no single answer, and we don't rank brands. For most South Florida driving, the choice is between an EV-specific touring or all-season tire, a regular all-season tire and a summer performance tire. Weigh wet grip, tread life, noise and range, and always match the size, load index and speed rating your Tesla specifies.
Do I need all-season tires on a Tesla in South Florida?
Not for snow. Michelin says summer tires are designed for warm conditions above 45°F and deliver their best dry and wet grip in that range. All-season tires trade some of that for a wider temperature range and, often, longer tread life. Think about whether you'll drive the car somewhere cold.
Are EV-specific tires worth it on a Tesla?

chunks.title: Best Tire Types for Teslas in South Florida Heat and Rain
chunks.text:
Questions people ask
They're designed around what EVs ask of a tire: weight, instant torque, low noise and low rolling resistance. Michelin notes that tires tuned mainly for range can trade away some grip or tread life, so read what each EV tire was designed to prioritize.
Do tires affect a Tesla's range?
Yes. Rolling resistance is the energy a tire uses as it rolls, and EV makers specify low rolling resistance tires to help range. Under-inflated tires also roll with more resistance, so keeping pressure at the placard figure matters too.
